_readme: Every assumption the A03 sizing calculator uses. An assumption is any object with a `value`: it must carry unit, source, verified and owner, and a [[VERIFY]] note while verified is false. Edit this file, then run `node tools/build-config.mjs` to regenerate config.js and re-inline it into index.html. Bromic product values mirror data/product-facts.json and stay verified:false until Mike Clifford signs off.

open.label: Open
open.hint: No roof over the heated area.

factor.source: Assumption: no overhead cover, so no 'heat cloud' and more wind exposure (Planning Guide v1.2 Step 01, qualitative only)
factor.verify: [[VERIFY: coverage derate for fully open spaces — Mike Clifford]]

partial.label: Partially covered
partial.hint: A pergola, umbrella or part roof over some of the area.

factor.source: Assumption: Lookbook coverage treated as the partially covered reference case
factor.verify: [[VERIFY: which setting the Lookbook coverage figures assume — Mike Clifford]]

covered.label: Covered
covered.hint: A solid roof, with walls on some sides.

factor.source: Assumption: a cover traps a 'heat cloud' that adds a convective boost (Planning Guide v1.2 Step 01, qualitative only)
factor.verify: [[VERIFY: coverage uplift for covered spaces — Mike Clifford]]

mild.label: Mild
mild.hint: Evenings you heat are usually above about 50°F.

factor.source: Assumption. Planning Guide v1.2 Step 05 says colder states may need more heaters for the same space (its example: 2 heaters in California, 3 in Massachusetts for 20 × 10 ft)
factor.verify: [[VERIFY: climate derate factors and the temperature bands that define them — Mike Clifford]]

cool.label: Cool
cool.hint: Evenings you heat are usually about 40–50°F.

cold.label: Cold
cold.hint: Evenings you heat are often below about 40°F.

factor.source: Assumption (see mild). Note: the Planning Guide's example (2 gas heaters for 200 ft² in California) implies a layout or overlap allowance this tool does not model

controls.app_note: Wi-Fi and app features require compatible Affinity Smart-Heat controls, sold separately.
controls.integration_note: Works with Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Control4, Crestron and Lutron. Compatibility varies by system and may need additional integration hardware or configuration.

disclaimers.coverage: Coverage is approximate and varies by heater model, mounting height, environment and installation conditions (Lookbook 2026). This is a first estimate, not a design.
disclaimers.code: Electric heaters in the US follow ANSI/NFPA 70 (NEC) and gas heaters ANSI Z223.1/NFPA 54. Confirm every installation with your local building authority and a licensed electrician or gas fitter.
